guidance.whenNotToUse: 1.  Avoid overloading buttons on one page or proximity of two or more buttons to each other, which may create visual overload and difficulty in making decisions. 2. When you wish to direct the user to additional information, you must use the link and avoid using the button. Recommendations for buttons from the government language characterization guide: It is recommended to read the dedicated instructions for the buttons in the government language characterization guide -
a11y: Contrast Ratio: Ensure the button has sufficient color contrast. The contrast ratio must be at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. You can find the guidelines for color contrast in WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum).

Keyboard Navigation: The button must be fully accessible via keyboard. Ensure that the button can receive focus using the Tab key and can be activated with the Enter or Space keys. This complies with WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.1.1: Keyboard.
Focus Indicators: When the button is focused, there must be a visible focus indicator to help users with keyboard navigation. This is required by WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.7: Focus Visible.
Accessible Name: For icon-only buttons, always provide an aria-label that clearly describes the button's function. This adheres to WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value.

Avoid Redundant ARIA Attributes: When using semantic elements like <button>, avoid using redundant ARIA attributes like role="button" or tabindex, which are already inherently included. This follows best practices outlined in WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.1: Parsing.
